routing_warnings.description: The concrete runtime observation is a plumbing leak; the broad statement that everything functions as expected does not specifically establish dual-station operation.
The freelancer specifically claims that the plumbing was fixed, not that dual-station operation was implemented or verified.
The target-specific content concerns repaired plumbing and absence of leaks; the statement about filming everything working is only a future plan.
The implementation claim specifically establishes that the plumbing is repaired and functional.
The requested smaller and thinner whisk is a hardware-configuration change rather than a change to the beverage-result Requirement.
The concern is preservation of froth during dispensing through the spout, not production of froth during mixing.
The concrete runtime observation is a plumbing leak; the broad statement that everything functions as expected does not specifically verify matcha mixing quality.
The fix claim explicitly concerns the plumbing rather than matcha mixing quality.
The requested downward-pouring direction changes spout geometry rather than valve-control behavior.
The concrete observed plumbing leak belongs to the leak-free plumbing Requirement; the broad statement that everything functions does not specifically verify dispensing.
The plumbing repair claim addresses leak containment rather than controlled button-operated dispensing.
The cracked fitting explains the plumbing leak and belongs to the leak-free plumbing Requirement.
The no-leak claim is specific to repaired plumbing; the remaining statement about everything working is too broad to verify this target.
The claim that plumbing is repaired and functional does not specifically establish button actuation or controlled dispensing flow.
The request for a gravity-based dispensing method concerns the dispensing mechanism rather than the spout's physical geometry or orientation.
The measured spout height establishes cup clearance beneath the spouts and is better routed to the raised cup-clearance platform Requirement.
The removable panels and access to motors and internals primarily support the separate maintenance-access Requirement.
The observed cracked-plumbing leak is runtime failure evidence for leak-free plumbing, not sanitation of the fluid path.
The claim that the plumbing leak was fixed belongs to the leak-free plumbing Requirement.
The no-leaks claim concerns liquid containment rather than cleaning or sanitation.
The claim that the plumbing is repaired and functional belongs to the leak-free plumbing Requirement.

The plumbing leak reported during testing belongs to the leak-free plumbing Requirement; the same message's sturdiness statement repeats the structural verification already established without a distinct structural transition.
The requested beige color for the platform is a visual color-scheme requirement rather than a change to its cup-clearance function.
The requested matching font color belongs to branding and visual detailing rather than the functional platform requirement.
The request that the buttons be functional is tied to the revised pouring design and does not clearly identify the main power control.
The preference for the rendering-style power button concerns cosmetic DJ-style control detailing rather than power-control behavior or placement.
The requested light around the power button is decorative lighting rather than main power-interface behavior.
This message changes the base logo and typography rather than the beige-and-green color scheme.
The requested silver controls and measurement details concern DJ-style control detailing rather than the target color scheme.
The requested base height and edge-to-edge fit primarily define the independently tracked cup-clearance platform rather than the general CAD deliverable.
The client's removable-spout request is a functional cleaning behavior and should not be absorbed into the general CAD Requirement.
The completed on/off slot is a target-specific implementation claim for the main power interface rather than for completion of the CAD deliverable.
The requested motor-speed and torque behavior belongs to the independent variable-speed motor-drive Requirement.
The requested whisk material, durability, consistency, and foam-quality behavior belongs to the whisk-configuration Requirement.
The clean solenoid-operated pour and no-sputtering behavior belongs to the controlled-dispensing Requirement.
The minimal-splash and splash-guard expectations belong to the splash-control Requirement.
The no-dripping and no-leakage expectations belong to the leak-free plumbing Requirement.
The request for easily removable bowls belongs to the bowl-removal Requirement rather than the BOM artifact.
The higher-RPM splash-proof operation clauses independently affect the splash-control Requirement.
The requested smooth solenoid flow independently affects the controlled-dispensing Requirement.
The higher-rated controllers and 50A power supply also provide implementation evidence for electrical power capacity.
The request to retain the wiring layout for possible long-term use concerns preservation of the documentation set rather than creation criteria for the wiring plan.
The cursive K marking is owned by the narrower K-marked dispense-button Requirement.
The freelancer's commitment to add a K to each button concerns the narrower button-marking Requirement.
The beige color selection specifically modifies the K button markings.
The client's approval to select suitable LEDs concerns decorative lighting rather than DJ control detailing.
